cases.purpose: An Envelope with only a closed exemption has no assessment group record.
One atomic unit creates basis and a zero-valued assessment record.
A cumulative basis below 2,000 rounds to zero.
The first 2,000 atomic units produce one assessment unit.
Basis 2,001 produces one assessment unit and one unit of remainder.
The unsigned 64-bit maximum is evaluated without floating point or multiplication.
The minimum portable arithmetic domain includes the unsigned 128-bit maximum.
Two fills in one Scope telescope and the second fill realizes the previous remainder.
Four equal fills in one Scope produce the same final assessment as one combined fill.
Two source debits in one group aggregate before rounding.
Different assessment Principals remain independent rounding groups.
Unlike assets remain independent and are never summed into one onchain basis.
One external Principal debit is assessed once even when the route has internal legs.
A segregated unused origin Refund reduces 2,500 basis units to 2,000.
A one-unit exact reversal reduces 2,000 basis units below the first boundary.
A fully refunded applicable debit emits a zero-valued assessment record.
Builder and external-tax disclosures inside one gross debit are not added again.
An ordinary LP deposit remains applicable unless a closed objective exemption proves otherwise.
A fungible payment for a non-fungible asset is assessed without oracle-valuing the NFT.
The Protocol Assessment leg does not recursively increase basis.
A separate fee-funding Principal does not change the assessment group or basis.
A separately authenticated sponsor may fund one exact assessment tuple without changing its basis Principal.
Sponsor authority for another assessment Scope cannot fund this group.
A sponsor cannot fund more gross assessment than its exact authorization permits.
A sponsor claim cannot use an authorization evidence reference that Core did not authenticate.
A fill cannot pair authenticated evidence with a different fee-funding Scope ID.
A fill cannot substitute another fee-funding Principal for the Principal authenticated by evidence.
One Envelope cannot contain the same canonical assessment group twice.
External withholding cannot exceed the gross Protocol Assessment debit.
A debit occurrence identity cannot be reused across stored fills in one Scope.
A Refund occurrence identity cannot be reused across stored fills in one Scope.
An effect occurrence identity cannot be reused by distinct assessment groups sharing one Scope.
One Authorization Scope under one Core and Constitution cannot bind multiple assessment Principals.
A Refund cannot exceed its originating debit.
One Refund occurrence cannot be applied twice.
A Refund must reference a debit in the same group and fill provenance set.
Mixed or unrelated inventory cannot be presented as a basis-reducing Refund.
Two effect occurrences cannot share one debit identity.
Stored fills must have a strictly increasing sequence.
A later compensating credit cannot retroactively reduce the basis of a committed Fill.
A binding claiming the minimum portable arithmetic domain rejects overflow rather than wrapping.
A cached cumulative assessment must equal cumulative basis divided by 2,000.
Core rejects rather than clipping an assessment above the signed ceiling.
A positive assessment that funds zero spendable credit rejects the complete Envelope.
A failure after calculation cannot commit basis, transfer, liability, or Receipt state.
